claim:
Let \(1<q<2\), \(0<\omega<1\), and let \(X=d^{(2)}(\omega,q)\) be the real two-dimensional Lorentz sequence space
\[
\|(x_1,x_2)\|_X=\bigl((x_1^*)^q+\omega(x_2^*)^q\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where \(x_1^*\ge x_2^*\ge0\) is the decreasing rearrangement of \((|x_1|,|x_2|)\). Put
\[
\rho=\omega^{1/(2-q)}.
\]
Then the dual space has exact Ptolemy constant
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X^*)
=
(1+\rho^2)^{(2-q)/q}
\max\left\{1,\frac{2}{(1+\omega)^{2/q}}\right\}.
\]
This is exactly the known value of \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)\). Consequently,
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(d^{(2)}(\omega,q)\right)
=
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(d^{(2)}(\omega,q)^*\right)
\]
for every \(0<\omega<1\) and every \(1\le q<\infty\).
integrity: The dual norm is derived directly from the defining constrained maximization. The Euclidean comparison is globally optimized in the ordered ratio, and two explicit Ptolemy triples attain the two weight regimes. No finite computation is used as a substitute for the quantified proof.
scientific_limitations: The new exact calculation is restricted to real two-dimensional Lorentz spaces with \(0<\omega<1\) and \(1<q<2\). The all-\(q\) duality statement also uses previously known endpoint and \(q\ge2\) cases. No assertion is made for dimensions above two or for longer weight vectors.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant of dual two-dimensional Lorentz spaces below exponent two
